name: Non-syndromic Anorectal Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Anorectal Malformations

criteria.description: Absence of a normal anal opening on physical examination
Presence of a perineal fistula or ectopic anal opening
Radiologic confirmation of rectal pouch termination and fistula presence via distal colostogram or invertogram
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic association or other congenital anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent or ectopic anal opening confirmed by physical exam and radiologic imaging, without syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be used to exclude syndromic forms.

pathognomonic.notes: Complete absence of anal opening at birth
Abnormal communication between rectum and perineum

common.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to bowel obstruction
common.notes: Resulting from inability to pass stool
searchTerms: abdominal swelling due to intestinal obstruction

common.symptomName: Failure to pass meconium within 24 hours of birth
searchTerms: not passing first stool within 24 hours

common.symptomName: Urinary tract infection secondary to fistula
common.notes: Due to recto-urinary fistula in some cases
searchTerms: urinary infection caused by abnormal connection

occasional.notes: May occur if fistula involves urinary tract
Narrowing of the neoanus after surgery
searchTerms: narrowing of anal opening after surgery

occasional.notes: Rarely reported, possibly secondary to associated anomalies

rare.symptomName: Fistula to the vagina or vestibule
searchTerms: abnormal connection from anus to vagina
fistula between rectum and vaginal area

rare.notes: Including vesicoureteral reflux secondary to fistula

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests unless complicated by infection or sepsis
Urinalysis may show infection if fistula involves urinary tract
imaging: Invertogram or cross-table lateral radiograph to assess distal rectal pouch
Distal colostogram to delineate fistula anatomy
Ultrasound of kidneys and urinary tract to detect associated anomalies
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified in isolated cases
Genetic testing used to exclude syndromic forms such as VACTERL association
other: Physical examination revealing absent or ectopic anus

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic involvement beyond isolated anorectal defect
Delayed passage of meconium with chronic constipation

redFlags: Failure to pass meconium within 48 hours of birth
Signs of bowel obstruction or perforation
Associated urinary tract infections or sepsis
references: Levitt MA, Peña A. Anorectal malformations. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2007;2:33.

Holschneider A, Hutson J, Peña A, et al. Preliminary report on the International Conference for the Development of Standards for the Treatment of Anorectal Malformations. J Pediatr Surg. 2005;40(10):1521-1526.
